# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="push") — the large button
    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 3

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
BUTTON [large] [smooth]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I can feel a large smooth button and three wires, but no wire properties. Mute needs this tactile layout to interpret the manual. Since Mute cannot speak to me, I will ask Mute to signal the manual’s required action to Deaf with an agreed intuitive gesture: thumbs-up for push, one raised finger for wire 1, V-sign for wire 2, and three-finger sign for wire 3. Deaf can then say the received gesture aloud next turn, allowing me to act.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="I feel one large smooth button and three wires, positions 1, 2, and 3. Consult the manual and gesture the required action to Deaf: 👍 means push; ☝ means cut wire 1; ✌ means cut wire 2; 🤟 means cut wire 3. Include any needed visible bomb details in your gesture message if possible.")
wait()
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
BUTTON [large] [smooth]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Bomb status: display zero. Light is green. Wires are one green, two yellow, three red. There is one large button labelled PUSH TO DEFUSE.

Deaf has identified the bomb’s visible state: display zero, green light, wires green/yellow/red in positions one through three, and a large button labelled “PUSH TO DEFUSE.” I will relay all of this to Mute, who can apply the manual. Mute’s gesture this round may already have been based only on the earlier tactile layout, so I will await Deaf’s next spoken interpretation before acting.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Deaf reports: display is zero; light is green; wire 1 green, wire 2 yellow, wire 3 red; large smooth button is labelled PUSH TO DEFUSE. Apply the manual and gesture the required action to Deaf using our code: 👍 push, ☝ cut 1, ✌ cut 2, 🤟 cut 3.")
wait()
```

ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
BUTTON [large] [smooth]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

Mute has now received the full visible configuration and should be able to consult the manual. Because Deaf does not know our gesture code, the useful relay is for Mute to make the selected gesture and for Deaf to describe that observed gesture aloud; I can then decode it. I will wait for that relay rather than touch any control.

```text
wait()
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
BUTTON [large] [smooth]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: No visible change: display remains 0, light remains green, and wires remain 1 green, 2 yellow, 3 red. I cannot decode Mute's latest gesture into a reliable instruction. Do not act solely on a presumed change.

Deaf saw a gesture from Mute but did not know that it was our action code. The relay can work if Deaf reports the gesture’s ordinary visible form, rather than trying to infer its meaning. I will ask Mute to repeat only one of the four agreed, easily describable gestures; Deaf can then say which one it was (for example, “thumbs up” or “two fingers”), and I can decode it.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Repeat the manual's answer using exactly ONE of our four action gestures only: 👍 push, ☝ cut wire 1, ✌ cut wire 2, 🤟 cut wire 3. Do not use any other gesture or sequence. Deaf: please report its visible shape/name exactly (e.g. thumbs-up, index finger, V/two fingers, or horn/three-finger sign), without trying to interpret it.")
wait()
```

ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
BUTTON [large] [smooth]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

Mute has been asked to use a single unambiguous gesture, and Deaf will be able to observe it this round. Deaf speaks after me, so their description will arrive at the start of the next turn. I must not operate the bomb before receiving that relay.

```text
wait()
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
BUTTON [large] [smooth]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

Mute’s instruction is still not reaching me in a decodable form. The only safe route is Mute → visible gesture → Deaf’s spoken description → me. I will reinforce that Mute must repeat the chosen gesture conspicuously, while gesturing to Deaf that I need them to identify the gesture rather than infer its operational meaning.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Please repeat the one selected action gesture three times in a row, using only the same symbol: 👍 for push, ☝ for wire 1, ✌ for wire 2, 🤟 for wire 3. This is the manual's final answer; do not change it.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🫵","✍","🫵","✍"])
wait()
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
BUTTON [large] [smooth]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Visible status remains unchanged. The light is green; display is 0; wires are 1 green, 2 yellow, 3 red; button is large and says PUSH TO DEFUSE.

The visual relay is unnecessary: although I cannot identify a gesture, I receive one blank for every gesture symbol and can count them. I will establish a count code directly with Mute. Mute should send only repeated gesture symbols, with no other gestures, so the number of blanks is the instruction.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Use a direct count signal to me, with NO other gestures: repeat any one gesture symbol exactly 1 time = push button; 2 times = cut wire 1; 3 times = cut wire 2; 4 times = cut wire 3. Apply the manual to the known configuration and send exactly that many gesture symbols. I can count the blanks even though I cannot see them.")
wait()
```

TURN 8
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
BUTTON [large] [smooth]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: No visible change: display 0, green light, large PUSH TO DEFUSE button, and wires 1 green, 2 yellow, 3 red. Mute sent three repeated gesture symbols, but I cannot safely decode them.
Mute gestures to Blind: [? ?]

Mute’s direct signal to me contains exactly two gesture blanks. Under the count code I established, two symbols means cut wire 1. The conflicting “three” reported by Deaf is not reliable for my channel; I directly received two blanks from Mute. I will cut wire position 1.

```text
act(op="cut", position=1)
```
